notes: The title is COMMENTS ON “PURSUING STACKS”. The correction list contains eleven entries, grouped seven before and four after Section 14 etc, with page and line references retained exactly.

The p3 comment compares cubical and simplicial sets. Numbered points give cartesian closure, a realisation equivalence involving Kan simplicial sets and CW-spaces, and a product statement explicitly qualified by the fine topology with respect to compact subsets.

Item 3 continues with the Dold-Kan theorem and A. Dress’s simplicial proof of the Serre spectral sequence, citing the writer’s paper with Heath, “Cogluing homotopy equivalences”. The syntax satisfies ... is homeomorphic to is preserved as typed.

The final paragraph mentions Massey’s use of the cubical method and Brown-Higgins’s methods. Its last sentence continues onto another sheet; this reading stops at the visible words in the. There is no date, page count, author name, or authorial page number here. Archive 12 is a comment only.

[S013-cartesian-closure; item 1] A and B separately checked cartesian closure by the exponential construction (Y^X)_n = Hom_sSet(Delta[n] × X,Y). Restriction is precomposition on Delta[n]. Evaluation at the identity simplex and the map induced by each simplex of Z give inverse correspondences between maps Z × X → Y and Z → Y^X. The main reader rechecked the evaluation/restriction compatibility and the inverse constructions. This verifies the stated closure claim at that level; it is not a check of the separate realisation or spectral-sequence claims.

[S013-dold-kan-grading; item 3] A and C checked the unqualified phrase chain complexes. The ordinary normalization construction has no negative degrees. In particular, the complex with Z only in degree -1 cannot be isomorphic to a normalized simplicial abelian group. The main reader rechecked this degree obstruction. Thus the usual Dold–Kan reading presupposes a nonnegative grading convention; that convention may be implicit, so the page is not called refuted. The ink has no degree qualifier and none is inserted.

The only supplied wording alternative concerns the abrupt satisfies … is homeomorphic junction. All three readers confirm the direct typed transition; it is an unchanged C-context decision, not a literal correction or removed uncertainty mark. No authorial question mark, à vérifier, or similar proof qualification appears on this sheet.

check_events.outcome: Checked the possible degree-range ambiguity in the unqualified phrase chain complexes. For normalization of a simplicial abelian group, degrees below 0 are zero because the simplicial indexing begins at 0. A chain complex with Z in degree -1 and zero elsewhere therefore cannot be isomorphic to such a normalized complex. Thus the stated equivalence needs a nonnegative convention if chain complexes might otherwise mean all integer-graded complexes. The conventional nonnegative interpretation remains possible, so this is a qualification check, not a refutation of the author's intended statement. No qualifier absent from the ink is supplied in reading.tex. Note N013.6.
